title: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch on the fight to split off models from agents
slides: Why does Vercel's CEO want to split models from agents?
Agents today bundle reasoning with execution tightly.
Rauch argues models should stay pure, agents should act.
Decoupling lets each layer evolve independently and faster.
Your next app's agent can swap models without rewriting.
thread_text:
1. Split models from agents?

Vercel's CEO argues bundling them is the bottleneck holding AI back.

2. Reasoning tied to execution

Agents today can't swap brains without breaking their hands.

3. Keep models pure

Let them think. Let agents act. Separate the two layers entirely.

4. Decouple to accelerate

Each layer evolves on its own clock, not stuck waiting for the other.

5. Swap models without rewrites

Take your current agent, swap its brain, and keep the actions. Test it this week.

instagram.caption:
If you build an AI agent, you can now swap its model without rewriting all the code.  

Vercel’s CEO argues agents today bundle thinking with doing — and that’s slowing everything down 🧠🔗⚙️. He wants the “model” layer kept pure (reasoning) and the “agent” layer to handle actions separately.  

Decoupling means each part updates at its own pace — no more waiting for the other to catch up 🧩.  

Your next app can test GPT-5 this week, then swap to Claude 6 without touching its actions.  

Which model are you locking your current agent into?
